Hi Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the trial (so we're all aligned):

Summary of ask
- Finova wants a constrained POC to validate retrieval-augmented answer quality for your investor FAQ flow, and to measure latency/cost at scale.

Proposed scope (what Redwood will deliver)
- Offline eval on a curated set of 500 canonical prompts + Finova edge cases
- 2-week online shadow run sampling ~10% of live traffic (no user-facing changes)
- Grading rubric for correctness, relevance, and safety; aggregated metrics dashboard

Success criteria (proposed)
- Primary: Answer accuracy (MRR/Top-1 correctness) improvement >= 15% vs current baseline
- Latency: 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for inference path
- Safety/Hallucination: documented hallucination rate <= 2% on review set
- Cost: projected per-1k-token inference cost within 20% of target number Elena shared

Owners
- Finova PM: Elena Ruiz (you) — provide test prompts, access to anonymized traffic sample, sign MOU
- Redwood CS: Marissa Cole — POC coordination and success tracking
- Redwood ML Eng: Aditya Rao — eval harness, shadow config, rubric implementation
- Account Exec: me (Sean) — commercial milestones and timeline

Timeline (draft)
- Mar 3: sign simple MOU + grant read-only access to traffic sample
- Mar 8Mar 15: offline eval & rubric iteration (deliver preliminary report)
- Mar 22Apr 5: 2-week shadow run + live metrics collection
- Apr 9: final results review + decision on rollout/path to prod

Attachments: finova-poc-mop.pdf (method of process), finova-eval-rubric.xlsx (draft rubric), redwood-shadow-config.yaml (shadow run config stub)

Ask: Please confirm owners and the timeline above, and attach the anonymized prompt sample by COB Monday (Mar 1) if possible.

Adding some technical detail on the eval methodology and the grading rubric so we're clear on offline vs online shadow tradeoffs.

Offline eval (controlled, fast iteration)
- Dataset: 500 canonical + 200 edge cases (held-out).
- Metrics: Top-1 accuracy, MRR, BLEU where applicable, response length distribution, and a safety tag (safe/unsafe/needs-review).
- Manual review: 100-sample audit for hallucination labeling; reviewers score on a 0-3 scale for correctness (0 wrong/unsafe, 1 partially correct, 2 mostly correct, 3 fully correct).
- Outcome: quick quantitative readout and prioritized failure modes for model/config changes.

Online shadow (real traffic, behavior & ops validation)
- Mode: forked requests go to Redwood but responses not surfaced to end users; we log model outputs, latencies, and retrieval traces.
- Sampling: start 5% -> 10% as Marissa suggested; run for 2 calendar weeks once stable.
- Observability: automatic alert if hallucination rate > 5% in a rolling 1-day window or if p95 latency > 500ms.
- Privacy: we will redact PII from logs and follow the data flow diagram Marissa will provide.

Grading rubric (how we'll surface results)
- Per-sample score vector: correctness (0-3), relevance (0-2), safety flag (0/1).
- Composite score = (correctness/3)*0.6 + (relevance/2)*0.3 - safety_flag*0.5. Range normalized to 0-1 for dashboards.
- Thresholds: any sample with composite < 0.4 flagged for immediate review; target average composite >= 0.65 for POC success.

I'll push a small script into the shared doc so Finova reviewers can replicate the scoring locally.

Aditya
